JUST FUTURE-PROOFING? GET THE EDITOR SAVE ONTO SWITCH 2 FIRST. The editor gives you Lua execution inside Seedsow Lullaby and access to the game's own save files. Install it now as a foothold that nintendo cannot take for when a future Artemis exploit is released. Follow the beginner installation guide to transfer the save. Once the transfer finishes, you can stop. Keep the game, its save, recovery slots and a backup. If you already have smileBasic, this is not neccesary!
Firmware checkpoint (2026-10-27): this preparation guide targets 23.0.1 on both consoles while it is current . If a newer firmware is released, stop before updating and read the firmware guidance . Future FS preparation can be affected even if the Lua editor still runs.
Write, save and run Lua inside Seedsow Lullaby on Switch 1 or Switch 2. The editor works with a controller and on-screen character grid, or a wired USB keyboard. It also edits text, hex and ordinary files in the game's own save storage.
Vibecoded: built with AI assistance and hands-on console testing. Expect rough edges.
For a first installation, download the Switch save ZIP and follow the steps below. You can use the editor entirely on the console afterward. Older releases name the PC bundle seedsow-lua-editor-VERSION.zip ; it serves the same role. GitHub's automatic Source code archives are for development.
For this installation route, start with a modded/hacked Switch 1 that can run homebrew and can complete Nintendo's online save transfer. Your Switch 2 does not need to be modded. A Switch 2 alone cannot perform the initial JKSV restore.
Use sysNAND/sysMMC throughout, not emuNAND/emuMMC. Download and transfer on stock; boot CFW on that same sysNAND only to back up and restore with JKSV. Stock and CFW sysNAND share the internal save; emuNAND has a separate save.
For the nearby/local transfer below, install the same Seedsow Lullaby demo on both consoles. The full game and an NSO membership are not required. Link the intended save user on each console to the same Nintendo Account . The account used to download the demo need not itself be that save user.
Download Seedsow-Lua-Editor-Save.zip . It is already built. You do not need Python, a clean autosave, developer hashes, the source bundle or a Raspberry Pi.
On Switch 1 in stock sysMMC , start New Game and hold R until normal dialogue. Release R , press ZL to open the save menu , then choose an empty slot and save. JKSV will only recognize the game for that user after you have made at least one save. Close the game, boot CFW sysMMC , and use JKSV to back up that user's save and restore the downloaded ZIP. Return to stock sysMMC . These boot modes use the same internal save storage.
On both consoles, use System Settings > Data Management > Transfer Your Save Data to move that user's demo save to Switch 2.
Load slot 1 on Switch 2, fully close and restart the game, then load it again. If you only want to prepare for later, stop here.
Follow the complete step-by-step installation guide . It covers JKSV installation, the SD card folders, backups, restoring and transfer. See the full-game setup . Online License controls game access; NSO Save Data Cloud is a separate, membership-based way to copy the same full-game save between consoles. A demo save cannot be transferred to the full game. If you own the digital full game, Online License lets the purchasing user launch it on Switch 1 while online without loading its virtual game card there. Restoring replaces the chosen save; keep your original backup. An existing editor installation does not need the starter restored over its saved programs.
Networking: both nearby/local transfer and NSO cloud backup require Nintendo connectivity and account verification. Nearby/local transfer still needs both consoles connected to Nintendo's servers. Blocking Nintendo servers beforehand can prevent it. Use stock sysNAND/sysMMC on Switch 1 for either transfer method, after restoring with JKSV under CFW on that same sysNAND. Using CFW on sysNAND is not ban-proof . See the guide before changing your setup. Once installed, editing, saving and running Lua require no Nintendo connection.
Compatibility evidence, title IDs and transfer requirements . No other game edition has been established as incompatible by this project.
Open slot 1, edit a program, then choose Save + publish into a user slot. Load that slot from the game's menu to run it again. Learn the console controls and keep recovery slots 1-3. Compatible editor updates can be installed in a fresh user slot later; see updates and recovery .
Fresh saves built from this source open the current editor directly in slot 1, including line movement, scrolling and a visible insertion cursor. Older installations can add it in a fresh user slot using the update guide . The 0.1.3 fresh-save build was reported working on console on 2026-10-27. That report does not establish a complete regression pass for every feature. Release 0.1.3 includes this editor in the prepared Switch save. Existing installations can keep their programs and use the update methods linked above.
The desktop companion works on Windows and has user-reported support on macOS. It sends files over your LAN to a Raspberry Pi, which acts as a Bluetooth controller. The console uses Bluetooth input; its Wi-Fi and Nintendo servers are not used for these uploads. This setup is optional; the editor also works directly on the console with its controller grid or a wired USB keyboard's text-entry dialog.
Airplane mode can stay ON, including during pairing. Enable only its Bluetooth/controller exception and leave console Wi-Fi OFF. Pairing, calibration and uploads do not require turning airplane mode off. Nintendo's initial official save transfer is a separate step that requires internet connectivity.
Download Seedsow-PC-Companion-and-Source-VERSION.zip , extract it and keep its folders together. The companion needs Python 3.10+ with Tcl/Tk and no pip packages.

Follow Pi setup , then send a file . Controller uploads are slow. Use the companion's estimate for the actual file; an editor update can take an hour or more. The 1 MiB file limit describes storage.
